outcome: Patient and Observer Scar Assessment Scale (POSAS)
cohort: The study included 30 women who had undergone a cesarean section, with 15 in the treatment group and 15 in the control group.
finding: Patients receiving manual therapy for cesarean scars showed statistically significant improvements in all analyzed scar characteristics, including reduced vascularity, hyperpigmentation, distortion, and scar height, as well as increased elasticity and pliability.
followup_time: 5 weeks (interval between initial and final scar evaluation)
